title: VLAN Configuration, Part 4: Hardening and Troubleshooting
labTitle: Lock it down, then fix it
labSub: VLAN security and a troubleshooting routine

scenes.narration: You can build V L A Ns in your sleep by now. This final part is about the two things that separate beginners from professionals. Locking the network down, and fixing it when it breaks. First, you'll block the two classic V L A N hopping attacks. Then you'll park every unused port somewhere harmless. Next, you'll learn a five step routine for tracking down faults. And you'll fix two real faults, plus one nasty gotcha.

items.t: Fix two real faults and one nasty gotcha

scenes.heading: Two ways in
scenes.narration: Attackers have two favourite tricks to jump from one V L A N to another. In the first, they trick a switch port into becoming a trunk, by pretending to be another switch. In the second, they stack two tags on one frame, so the outer tag is stripped and the inner one is used. Both tricks are stopped by a few simple settings, which we'll apply now.

items.real: Access mode, no DTP, unused native VLAN

scenes.narration: We'll start with the trunk between the switches. First, we turn off trunk negotiation with switchport nonegotiate, so nobody can talk a port into trunking. Then we move the native V L A N to the unused V L A N ninety nine, so no user port can ever share it. Show interfaces switchport confirms trunk mode, negotiation off, and native V L A N ninety nine.

steps.note: No user ports in VLAN 99 = no double tagging.
Check mode, negotiation and native VLAN.

scenes.narration: Now the user ports and the unused ports. Every user port gets switchport mode access, which switches negotiation off for that port. Unused ports are an open door, so we create a black hole V L A N, ninety nine nine, that goes nowhere. We put all the unused ports in it, and shut them down. Show interfaces status gives a quick overview. Unused ports are disabled in V L A N nine nine nine.

steps.note: Never leave a user port on 'dynamic auto'.
A VLAN with no gateway, nowhere to go.

out: Port      Name   Status       Vlan  Duplex Speed Type

scenes.heading: The 5-step routine
scenes.narration: When something breaks, don't guess. Follow the same five steps, in order. First, is the port in the right V L A N? Use show V L A N brief. Second, is the port up? Use show interfaces status. Third, does the trunk carry that V L A N? Use show interfaces trunk. Fourth, do both ends match on mode and native V L A N? Look for C D P warnings. And fifth, only then check addresses and the gateway.

Now a real fault. PC three can't reach PC one, across the trunk. Step one. On SW two, show V L A N brief shows fast ethernet zero slash one is still in V L A N one. Someone forgot to assign it. We fix that in two lines. Still failing? Step three. Show interfaces trunk shows only V L A N twenty is allowed across. We add V L A N ten, using the word add, so we don't wipe the list. Now the ping from PC three to PC one works.

steps.note: PC3's port is in the wrong VLAN.

out: 1    default             active    Fa0/1, Fa0/3, Fa0/4, Fa0/5

steps.note: VLAN 10 is missing from the allowed list.
Fixed. Two faults, found by following the routine.

scenes.narration: And here's the nasty gotcha. Say someone deletes V L A N twenty, because it looks unused. The ports aren't moved. They stay assigned to a V L A N that no longer exists. Everything on that port goes dead, with no warning. The fix is simply to create the V L A N again.

steps.note: Deleting a VLAN doesn't touch the ports.
The port is orphaned, and silently dead.

lines.c: show interfaces fa0/2 switchport | include Access Mode

steps.note: Re-create the VLAN and it comes back.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three professional habits. Set every port explicitly, as access or trunk. Move the ports out first, then delete the V L A N. And troubleshoot in the same order every time.

items.right: Set every port explicitly: access or trunk

items.wrong: Deleting a VLAN that has ports
items.right: Move the ports first, then delete the VLAN
Follow the same five steps every time

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva VLAN security lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Turn off negotiation, and use an unused native V L A N. Park unused ports in a black hole V L A N, shut down. And follow the five step routine, instead of guessing. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva VLAN security lab.
